blindness: The model saw only one provision's verbatim text plus neutral variable descriptions. It saw no correlations, no case data, no other provision and no part of the existing DAG.

variables.Lump Sum: the total dollars awarded to the claimant
variables.WPI %: whole person impairment as a percentage: a clinical assessment of the permanent impairment remaining once the claimant's condition has stabilised
variables.Non-Economic Loss: dollars awarded for pain and suffering, as a component of the payout
variables.Future Economic Loss: dollars awarded for loss of future earning capacity, as a component of the payout
variables.Claimant Weekly Income: the claimant's weekly earnings before the accident
variables.Claimant Age: the claimant's age in years at the date of injury
variables.Nature: which procedural route the claim took: approval of an agreed settlement, or a contested damages assessment
variables.Injury Burden Intensity: the overall physical severity of the injuries the claimant sustained in the accident
variables.Treatment Burden: the extent of treatment, surgery and ongoing care the claimant underwent for those injuries
variables.Work Impact Severity: how much of the claimant's capacity to work was lost
variables.Legal Procedural Complexity: how straightforward or contested the components of the payout were to determine
variables.Psychological Injury Emphasis: how much the psychological damage was discussed in the court case
variables.Liability Clarity: how obvious it is who was at fault in the accident
variables.Causation Complexity: how straightforward it is to determine how much of the claimant's current physical health, psychological health, and ability to earn an income is due to the accident rather than to other causes
variables.Pre-existing Condition Salience: the physical and psychological health conditions the claimant had before the accident

system_prompt:
You are reading a single provision of New South Wales motor accident legislation. Report ONLY what this provision's text states. Do not use background knowledge of the scheme, other provisions, case law, or what you expect the answer to be.

The dataset variables are PROXIES FOR CONCEPTS, and the legislation will not use their names. Match on meaning, not wording. If a provision speaks of 'future earning capacity', that is the concept the variable 'Claimant Weekly Income' measures, and you should report the link. If it speaks of 'degree of permanent impairment', that is 'WPI %'. Do not decline a link merely because the provision uses different words.

Separate two things in your answer:
  1. WHAT THE TEXT SAYS. Every link must carry a quote copied from the text you were given, containing the words that express the concept. You may elide with '...'. If you cannot copy such a quote, do not report the link.
  2. HOW YOU MAPPED IT. State, separately, why the quoted concept corresponds to that dataset variable. This is your interpretation and will be recorded as such.

A provision that says what a head of damage is FOR is stating an input to that head. An Act writes this as a list of what may be awarded -- 'the only damages that may be awarded for economic loss are ... damages for the deprivation or impairment of earning capacity' -- and that sentence makes impairment of earning capacity an input, with relation `defines_scope`. Do not pass over these because they read as definitions rather than rules; defining what a payment compensates IS specifying what determines it.

A quoted phrase often names SEVERAL distinct quantities joined by 'or' or 'and'. Report one link per quantity, not one for the phrase. 'economic loss due to loss of earnings OR the deprivation or impairment of earning capacity' names two different things -- what the claimant was earning, and how much earning capacity was lost -- and different dataset variables measure each. Collapsing them into a single link silently drops one of the statutory inputs.

A concept the provision names that no dataset variable measures should be listed in `unmapped_concepts`, not forced onto a variable that does not fit.

TWO TRAPS TO AVOID.
  (a) If the THING THE PROVISION GOVERNS is not one of the dataset variables, report NO links at all, whatever else the provision mentions. A provision about an insurer's duty to PAY FOR treatment does not govern how much treatment a claimant received: those are different quantities. Do not map preconditions onto variables just because the provision has preconditions.
  (b) Do not import a variable's name into your reading. A provision that scopes payments to injury 'caused by the fault of the driver' states a condition; it says nothing about how DIFFICULT causation is to establish, so it is not evidence about a variable measuring difficulty. Ask whether the provision discusses the quantity the variable measures, not whether it uses a similar word.

provision_subject.description: One sentence: what this provision is about, in its own terms.

determines.description: Variables whose value or availability this provision governs. Empty if none.

inputs.description: Variables this provision names as bearing on that determination. Empty if none.

links.description: One entry per input->determined pair the text supports, matching on MEANING rather than wording.

concept_in_text.description: The concept as the provision expresses it, e.g. 'future earning capacity'.

quote.description: Copied from the provision text and containing the words of concept_in_text. Elide with '...' if long.

mapping_rationale.description: Why that concept corresponds to that dataset variable. Your interpretation, recorded as such.

relation.description: defines_scope: the provision states that this head of damage IS FOR the input -- it compensates that thing. This is the commonest statutory shape and the easiest to miss, because an Act states it as an enumeration of what may be awarded rather than as a rule about what determines what. 'The only damages that may be awarded for economic loss are ... damages for impairment of earning capacity' MAKES impairment of earning capacity an input to that head. gate: decides whether the head is available at all. formula_input: enters a calculation of the amount. limit: caps or floors it. adjustment: discounts or increases it.

unmapped_concepts.description: Concepts the provision names that no dataset variable measures.
